questions.stem: A cumulative frequency table shows: ≤10 (5), ≤20 (18), ≤30 (35), ≤40 (48), ≤50 (52). How many values are in the class 20 < x ≤ 30?
questions.explanation: Frequency for 20 < x ≤ 30 = cumulative at 30 minus cumulative at 20 = 35 - 18 = 17. A common error is reading the cumulative frequency (35) as the frequency for the class.

questions.stem: A cumulative frequency graph for 80 students shows: at x = 40, CF = 20; at x = 60, CF = 60. Estimate the median.
questions.explanation: Median is at the 40th value (80/2 = 40). CF = 20 at x = 40, and CF = 60 at x = 60. The 40th value is between these. 40th is 20 above CF of 20, and the interval 40-60 covers 40 values. So median ≈ 40 + (20/40) x 20 = 40 + 10 = 50.

questions.stem: For 60 data values, what cumulative frequency values should you read to find the lower quartile (Q1) and upper quartile (Q3)?

options.text: Q1 at 15th value, Q3 at 45th value
Q1 at 20th value, Q3 at 40th value
Q1 at 15th value, Q3 at 30th value
Q1 at 30th value, Q3 at 45th value

questions.explanation: Q1 is at n/4 = 60/4 = 15th value. Q3 is at 3n/4 = 3(60)/4 = 45th value. These positions are read from the cumulative frequency axis to find the corresponding data values on the x-axis.

questions.stem: A cumulative frequency diagram for 100 values gives Q1 = 24 and Q3 = 42. What is the interquartile range?
questions.explanation: IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 42 - 24 = 18. The IQR measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data. Option (a) adds instead of subtracting. Option (b) is the median of the quartile values.

questions.stem: From a cumulative frequency graph of 80 students' marks, the median is 55 and the IQR is 22. Q1 = 44. What percentage of students scored more than 66?
questions.explanation: Q3 = Q1 + IQR = 44 + 22 = 66. Q3 means 75% of values are at or below 66. Therefore 25% scored more than 66. This is 0.25 x 80 = 20 students.
